sentences.text: The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 18.7.2020.

Shivaraju vs Arun Kumar .T on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28827475/
1 2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 18.7.2020 at about 5.00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing No. KA-42-EA- 2939 to go to Sankigatta to Virupapura and when he reached near Hullenahalli- Sugganahalli road, Goripalya, Thippasandra Hobli, Magadi Taluk, the driver of tractor bearing No. KA-06-TB-3844 came from Virupapura main road in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries over head, left hand left leg and all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Vinayaka Hospital, Tumkur and after first aid he was shifted o Kanva Hospital, Nandini Layout.

Later he was shifted to Vinayak Hospital, Tumkur wherein he was admitted as inpatient and he has spent Rs.10,00,000/-
towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as mason and earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/-
with interest.
3. After service of notices, respondent No.1 remained absent hence, placed exparte.

Respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the tractor bearing No. KA-06-TB-3844 and the liability of this respondent if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that, the accident was occured due to negligence on the part of the petitioner himself and there is no negligence on the part of driver of the tractor.
Further the respondent No.2 contended that the driver of the tractor was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Further denied the age, avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:

sentences.text:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of tractor bearing No. KA-06-TB-3844 by its driver, in RTA took place on 28.07.2020 at about 5.00 p.m. on Hullenahalli, Suggnahalli road,
Goripalya, Thippasandra Hobli, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagara District?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what amount and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and case is posted for further chief examination.
Thereafter the petitioner filed IA No.3 under order 32 Rule 5 of CPC by praying for the natural guardian to represent the petitioner in this case.
The said IA is came to be allowed as per the order dated 18.10.2022 and thereby the natural guardian is permitted to represent the petitioner.
The wife of the petitioner is examined as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 14.
Dr. Veeresha U. Mathad., who is working as Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon at Sri. Lakshmi Multispeciality Hospital, Bangalore is examined as PW.3, through him got marked Ex.P15 to 17.
Also examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N., who is working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Centre as PW.4 and got marked documents at Ex.P18 & 19.
In spite of sufficient opportunities, the respondents did not chose to adduce evidence.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.

That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the natural guardian of the petitioner/
wife filed her affidavit in lieu of-examination in-chief and examined as P.W.2.

In support of their case, the PW.1 produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, seizer mahazar, IMV report,
wound certificate and charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 7.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of Ex.P2 first information given by the brother of the petitioner who is with the petitioner at the time of alleged accident.

In the Ex.P2 it is alleged that when the petitioner was proceeding in the bike bearing No. KA-42- EA-2939, the tractor bearing No. KA-06-TB-3844 which came from opposite side in a rash and negligent manner and Shivaraju vs Arun Kumar .T on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28827475/
3 dashed against the bike of the petitioner.
10. After the registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the Ex.P3 spot mahazar was conducted.
On perusal of the contents of Ex.P3 spot mahazar therein, the accident is within three feet of the tar road from footpath.
Thus, it is found that the driver of the tractor bearing No. KA-06- TB-3844 has came to his right side and dashed against the petitioner who was proceeding in the left side.
The Ex.P5 is the IMV report wherein front and right side of the bike of the petitioner has got damaged and no damages are found on the tractor.
But as per Ex.P4 the front bumper of the tractor has got scratches.
This supported the case of the petitioner.

11. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 insurance company vehemently argues that there is an inordinate delay of 2 days in lodging the FIR and the same cannot be brushed aside lightly,
instead has to be construed as a circumstance showing that the case is an afterthought.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 also argued that as per IMV report there is no scratches found on the tractor bearing No. KA-06-TB- 3844, the said tractor is falsely implicated.
12. By considering the argument canvassed by both the parties no doubt that delay has to be explained in the petitions filed for the compensation.
But not every delay would move this court to view the case of the petitioners doubtfully.
Because there might be genuine circumstances that could have contributed to the delay.
In fact only if the delay is left unexplained the same needs to be viewed seriously.

No doubt in the facts of this case, the accident occurred on 18.7.2020 at about 5.00 p.m., but the FIR was lodged on 20.7.2020 at about 1.00 p.m. and hence it is evident that the FIR is lodged after one and half day of occurrence of the alleged accident.

But the informant of Ex.P2 has clearly narrated in Ex.P-2 complaint as to why the FIR was lodged belatedly by narrating that soon after the accident at 5.00 p.m. the petitioner Shivaraju was initially shifted to Vinayaka Hospital,
Tumkuru and thereafter shifted to Kanva Hospital, Bengaluru, as such they could not lodge the FIR immediately; and the said explanation offered by the informant for delaying the lodging of the FIR is plausible.
As per Ex.P6 wound certificate the petitioner Shivaraju has got haemmoraghic wounds in the brain and also severe head injury as per Ex.P8.
The endeavor of the family of the injured will be getting the treatment to the injured than thinking about the legal formalities.

Perhaps the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226, has observed thus:
"The purpose of lodging the FIR in motor accident cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.

entities.text: Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquillity of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if there is delay, the same deserve to be condoned.

In such Shivaraju vs Arun Kumar .T on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28827475/
4 circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons.

entities.text: Shivaraju vs Arun Kumar .T on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground."
(Emphasis supplied by me)
Hence the delay of one and half day, in the light of reasons assigned by the PW.1 and also as mentioned in the Ex.P2, complaint and it cannot be considered as inordinate.

13. It is interesting to note that no doubt the FIR was lodged belatedly, but in all the medical records, it is clearly mentioned that the history narrated to the doctors by the family of injured at the very first instance, as can be seen from Ex.P.6 wound certificate is that injuries were sustained in an RTA and the petitioner bought to the hospital at Bengaluru at 8.7.2020 at about 9.00 p.m. .
This version has not changed since then; and even in FIR the very same version can be seen.
In the Ex.P6 wound certificate, Ex.P8 discharge card and summaries also the occurrence of accident is also properly explained and it corroborates with the contents of Ex.P1 FIR and Ex.P.2 complaint.
Under such circumstances, this court is of the firm opinion that the delay is certainly backed by genuine reasons.

Moreover where the standard of proof required is preponderance of probabilities and the facts before the court probablizes the reasons assigned by PW.1 for delaying the lodging of the FIR as such this court cannot uphold the contention of the respondent No.2 regarding the delay by considering the condition of the petitioner after the accident.
14. In the accident cases, it is settled principle of law that "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" which means the things speaks itself, is the standing principle to know the nature of the accident.
Under this principle how the negligence has to be infer is considered.

In tort law, "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" principle that allows petitioners to meet their burden of proof with under which a court can infer negligence from the very nature of an accident or injury in the absence of direct evidence on how any defendant behaved in the context of tort litigation.

On perusal of Ex.P3- contents of mahazar with Ex.P5 IMV report wherein the damages of the vehicles involved in the accident is mentioned prima- facie shows the negligence on the part of the driver of tractor bearing No.KA-06-TB-3844.

As per the mahazar the accident is in the left side of the road in which the petitioner was proceeding and the driver of tractor came from opposite side and came to his right side and dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner.

If the driver of the tractor bearing No. KA-06-TB-3844 has not came to its right side, the said tractor is not going to get scratches and the bike of the petitioner is not going to be damaged in its front and right side as mentioned in Ex.P4- seizer mahazar.
Hence, by applying the said principle the negligence on the part of the driver of tractor bearing No.KA-06-TB-3844 is stands established.

15. Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P-7 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the tractor.

The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima- facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala Shivaraju vs Arun Kumar .T on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28827475/
5 and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus:
In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to supra and appreciated the same in the proper perspective and recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in the affirmative.

The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.

The registration of FIR and filing of the chargesheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants.
(Emphasis supplied by me)

16. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the inc ident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even here in this case the driver of the tractor is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the tractor and he was charge sheeted.

17. In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the tractor Shivaraju vs Arun Kumar .T

on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28827475/
6 bearing No.KA-06-TB-3844 resulting in petitioners sustaining injuries.
In the mahazar it is clearly mentioned that the accident place is within the three feet from the footpath towards the tar road.
Thus, the allegation of the respondent No.2 regarding the negligence on the part of the petitioner is also not sustained.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
18.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the driver of respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
This Court has already held Issue No.I in the affirmative which makes it more than obvious that the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

Needless to state the quantum of compensation which is awarded has to be proportionate to the nature of the injuries and the compensation has to be awarded by keeping in mind the pecuniary damages and non-pecuniary damages suffered by the injured- claimant.

By pecuniary damages this Court is referring to the actual loss sustained by the petitioner, which can be determined in terms of money, by taking into account the oral or documentary evidence whereas by non-pecuniary damages this Court is referring to the losses that the claimant has though suffered, but will not be able to prove for the reason that it can neither be calculated in terms of the money nor can it be proved leading documentary evidence.
Perhaps the non-pecuniary damages can be figured out by looking into the facts of each case by taking into account the nature of injuries and the aftermath.

It is required to be reminded to oneself that compensation in a case arising out of injury can never be granted on mathematical precision and invariably a good amount of guesswork is involved while determining the compensation in such cases.

Perhaps unlike in a fatal case, in a case involving bodily injury the victim is left to suffer throughout his life; and hence it becomes the bounden duty of the tribunal to award compensation to a victim of permanent disability so as to bring in sustainability and also to ensure that victim is not pushed to poverty.
19. In order to demonstrate the pecuniary loss suffered by him due to the injuries, the petitioner has led oral and documentary evidence.

The petitioner in their oral evidence has asserted on oath that immediately after the accident, the petitioner was taken to Immediately to Vinayaka Hospital,
Tumkur and after first aid he was shifted o Kanva Hospital, Nandini Layout.

Later he was shifted to Vinayak Hospital, Tumkur wherein he was admitted as inpatient and he has spent Rs.10,00,000/-
towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,

Further the petitioner has supported the said contention by producing Ex.P-5- wound certificate, Ex.P7 3 discharge summaries, Ex.P9medical bills, Ex.P.10 medical prescriptions 77 in numbers, Ex.P11 advance receipts, Ex.P12 lab reports 29 in nos. Ex.P13 X-ray films.

These medical documents along with discharge summaries pertaining to the petitioner which reveal indeed the petitioner underwent treatment at Vinayaka Hospital, Tumkur and after first aid he was shifted o Kanva Hospital, Nandini Layout.
Later he was shifted to Vinayak Hospital, Tumkur.

Further the petitioner has asserted that he has spent an amount of . 10,00,000/- towards his treatment and seeks to prove the same by producing the aforementioned documents and medical bills along with prescriptions which are exhibited at Ex.P-9 and 10, which reveal that petitioner indeed has sustained grievous injuries and has undergone treatment for the same.

7 20.
As regards the nature of injuries and the disability suffered the petitioner has produced Ex.P-8- discharge summaries along with the disability assessment affidavits filed by the PW.2 & 3 doctors.
It is keeping these facts in mind that the compensation has to be determined.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY :- At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 40 years.
Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P14 also shows that the petitioner was aged about 42 years at the time of accident.
The discharge summary also shows that the age of the petitioner as 42.

In the petition itself he has averred that he was admitted to Vinayak Hospital, Tumkur, after first aid he was shifted Kanva Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was admitted as inpatient for 20 days and again he was shifted to Vinayak Hospital, Tumkur.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P8 the petitioner sustained severe head injury, traumatic brain injury- DAI, left tibial condyle fracture extending into metaphysic with fasciotomy.
He underwent ORIF for left tibia with LCP with secondary suturing.

The evidence of the PW.3 who is a Senior Consultant Neuro Surgeon in his clinical examination found that the petitioner is conscious, obeys commands, His higher mental functions are impaired,
his memory is also impaired.
His MMSE score is 15 ( normal is 30).
Along with the said clinical examination the PW.2 also produced his report in this regard.

Regarding the present appearance and physical condition of the petitioner in his disability assessment affidavit, the PW.2 stated that the Speech of the petitioner is slurred, slow to speak, not clear, not able to understand spoken words and also stated that the petitioner is suffering with left Hemiparesis Regarding the movements of the upper limb and lower limb the PW.2 mentioned
that there is a Left foot drop present in the petitioner and the petitioner has tremors/ involuntary movements in hands.

Regarding the physical ability of the petitioner the PW.2 doctor deposed in his disability assessment affidavit that the petitioner is not able to get up or walk independently and requires support of other or walker.
The PW.2 doctor also conducted CT Scan of the brain on 9.1.2023 and reported that compare to earlier injuries all the brain injuries are healed.

Before giving disability assessment report the PW.2 also subjected the petitioner for detailed neuropsychological evaluation by the psychologist on 19.1.2023 and found that the petitioner IQ is 41- moderate mental retardation.

On IDEAS scale the scores are 13 which shows that the petitioner has 40-70% disability in the areas of self-care, interpersonal activities, communication &
understanding and work.

It is very important to note that in his report the PW.3 has specifically mentioned that the petitioner is suffering with moderate severe disability and unable to attend his own bodily needs without assistant and unable to walk unassisted.
It is very important that the evidence of PW.3 is subjected to cross-examination by the learned counsel for the respondent.
The petitioner sustained with head injury which resulted in traumatic brain injury.
After the accident when the petitioner shifted to hospital he was unconscious.

The discharge summaries and the conditions of the patients as mentioned in discharge summary Shivaraju vs Arun Kumar .T on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28827475/
8 supported the evidence of PW.3- doctor.
The respondents even after sufficient opportunities has not lead evidence in support of their contentions.
The respondents has not examined any other competent doctors to discard the evidence of the PW.3.
Hence, nothing is available on record to disbelieve the evidence of PW.3.
The evidence of PW.4 who is a orthopedic surgeon also assessed the disability.
The disability assessed by the PW.3 shows that the petitioner is unable to attend his own bodily needs without assistance.

By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the brain injuries sustained in the accident Rs.1,00,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P9, amounting to Rs.7,55,421/-.

As per the said medical bills, at SL. no. 4 & 6 amounting to Rs.2,530/- and Rs.935/- =
Rs.3,645/- is pertaining to some cafe bills wherein the name of the petitioner is not mentioned.
Hence, these two bills need to be rejected.

The other bills even though formally disputed by the respondent No.2, by considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the line of treatment this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner has spend the amount as shown in the bills.
Along with the bills the petitioner also produced lab reports and prescriptions of the hospital hence, no grounds are made out to discard these bills.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitle for the reimbursement of the same i.e.,
Rs.7,51,776/-, the said amount is rounded off to Rs.7,51,800/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was working as mason and earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any document.
Such being the case, it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.14,500/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2020.
As per the discharge summaries marked at Ex.P8- the petitioner was admitted to Vinayaka Hospital and Kanva Hospital and treated as inpatient for a period of 32 days.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,500 X 32 days = Rs.15,466/- during the laid up period, the said amount is rounded off to Rs.15,500/-.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner examined Dr.Veeresha U. Mathad, Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon at Sri. Lakshmi Multispeciality Hospital, Bangalore as PW.3, through him clinical notes, Neuropshycological assessment report and CT scan with report are marked at Ex.P15 to 17.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained SAH in bilateral frontal and parietal lobes, thin subdural haemorrhage left frontal convexity and diffuse axonal injury.
He underwent emergency fasciotomy and ORIF for left tibia with LCP on 21.7.2020.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
As per PW.3 the petitioner suffered permanent neurological disability of 74%.
As discussed above, the evidence of PW.2 shows that the condition of th epetitioner is not so fit to make any earnings.
When the person is unable to attend his own bodily needs we cannot expect that he is going to be a earning member in his family.
But it is very important to note that the person should not be left unattended or as a burden by the family.

9 In this regard, I rely on the reportable decision, in Civil Appeal No.2476/2019 in the case of M.R.Krishamurthi V/s New India Assurance Company Ltd., decided on 05.03.2019, the Hon'ble supreme court has held as follows, "We may now summarize the principles discussed above:
(i) All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.

entities.text: M.R.Krishamurthi V/s New India Assurance Company Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.

To put it differently, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability (except in a few cases, where the Tribunal on the basis of evidence, concludes that the percentage of loss of earning capacity is the same as the percentage of permanent disability).

(iii) The doctor who treated an injured claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard to the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.

(iv) The same permanent disability may result in different percentages of loss of earning capacity in different persons, depending upon the nature of profession,
occupation or job, age, education and other factors."

A perusal of the injuries sustained, treatment taken and in view of the citation referred above, it is considered that though the petitioner is having 74% permanent physical disability ,his avocational disability is 100% because the evidence of Pw.3 is clear that the petitioner is unable to attend his own bodily needs without assistance and unable to walk unassisted.
This situation is nothing but making this tribunal to hold that the petitioner is unable to earn or to live independently hence, this disability is considered at 100%.

Further the petitioner also examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N. Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Centre as PW.4, through him got marked clinical examination note and X-ray which are marked at Ex.P.18 & 19.
PW.4 stated that the petitioner sustained head injury with left tibial condyle fracture.
X-ray of left knee shows united proximal tibia fracture with implant in situ.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross- examination.
Further PW.4 has also stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants which may costs Rs.60,000/-.
The petitioner has produced his Aadhar card marked at Ex.P14, as per this document the year of birth of the petitioner is shown as 1978.
The accident was occurred in the year-2020.
So, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 42 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '14'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.14,500/- X 12 X 14 X100% =Rs.24,36,000/- which is the total loss of future income.

"It is now a well settled position of law that even in cases of permanent disablement incurred as a result of a motor-accident, the claimant can seek, apart from compensation for future loss of income,amounts for future prospects as well.

sentences.text: We have come across many orders of different tribunals and unfortunately affirmed by different High Courts, taking the view that the claimant is not entitled to compensation for future prospects in accident cases involving serious injuries resulting in permanent disablement.
That is not a correct position of law.
There is no justification to exclude the possibility of compensation for future prospects in accident cases involving serious injuries resulting in permanent disablement."
In the present case the petitioner has 100% avocational disability.
Hence in view of the citation referred above the petitioner is entitle for loss of future prospectus at 25% which comes to Rs.6,09,000/-.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE ; As per Ex.8 discharge summaries, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 32 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P6 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.

By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.75,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance as the petitioner has to be in need of further care till his death.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 32 days in the hospital.
During the said period the petitioner was uncoscious and he got brain injuries
hence, some attendant requires to be accompanied with the petitioner in the hospital.
Hence, for the period of 32 days the petitioner is entitled for attendant charges of Rs.1,000/- per day i.e, Rs.32,000/-.
For the reasons discussed above, is already held that the petitioner is suffering with 100% disability and unable to attend his own bodily needs.
This making this tribunal consider that the petitioner is in need of an attendant through out his life time.
The services of the family members cannot be considered graciously.
The petitioner should not be looked into as a burden to the family.
No evidence is lead by the petitioner to show that he has engaged an attendant by paying money.

In Kajal Vs. Jaidish Chand reported in 2020 SCC Online SC 127, it is held that it would be appropriate to adopt the system of multiplier to award the compensation under the head 'Attendant Charges' as the claimant would require the care of an attendant for the rest of his life.

sentences.text: Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him.
The petitioner sustained brain injuries and he is not fit enough like earlier and leading the life by depending on others.
This might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.
h)Towards future medical expenses: PW.4 stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants, which may costs Rs.60,000/-.
The petitioner has to be in continuous treatment through out his life time.
By looking to the nature of injuries sustained the treatment taken and need of future medical assistance the petitioner is entitle for Rs.50,000/- under this head.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 18.7.2020.
Further contended that, the accident was occured due to negligence on the part of the petitioner himself and there is no negligence on the part of driver of the tractor.
Thereafter the petitioner filed IA No.3 under order 32 Rule 5 of CPC by praying for the natural guardian to represent the petitioner in this case.

11. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 insurance company vehemently argues that there is an inordinate delay of 2 days in lodging the FIR and the same cannot be brushed aside lightly,
instead has to be construed as a circumstance showing that the case is an afterthought.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 also argued that as per IMV report there is no scratches found on the tractor bearing No. KA-06-TB- 3844, the said tractor is falsely implicated.
16. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the inc ident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Hence the delay of one and half day, in the light of reasons assigned by the PW.1 and also as mentioned in the Ex.P2, complaint and it cannot be considered as inordinate.
Under such circumstances, this court is of the firm opinion that the delay is certainly backed by genuine reasons.
Moreover where the standard of proof required is preponderance of probabilities and the facts before the court probablizes the reasons assigned by PW.1 for delaying the lodging of the FIR as such this court cannot uphold the contention of the respondent No.2 regarding the delay by considering the condition of the petitioner after the accident.
14. In the accident cases, it is settled principle of law that "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" which means the things speaks itself, is the standing principle to know the nature of the accident.
Under this principle how the negligence has to be infer is considered.
In tort law, "RES- IPSA LOQUITUR" principle that allows petitioners to meet their burden of proof with under which a court can infer negligence from the very nature of an accident or injury in the absence of direct evidence on how any defendant behaved in the context of tort litigation.
On perusal of Ex.P3- contents of mahazar with Ex.P5 IMV report wherein the damages of the vehicles involved in the accident is mentioned prima- facie shows the negligence on the part of the driver of tractor bearing No.KA-06-TB-3844.
As per the mahazar the accident is in the left side of the road in which the petitioner was proceeding and the driver of tractor came from opposite side and came to his right side and dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner.
If the driver of the tractor bearing No. KA-06-TB-3844 has not came to its right side, the said tractor is not going to get scratches and the bike of the petitioner is not going to be damaged in its front and right side as mentioned in Ex.P4- seizer mahazar.
Hence, by applying the said principle the negligence on the part of the driver of tractor bearing No.KA-06-TB-3844 is stands established.
15. Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P-7 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the tractor.
But it has recorded the finding in the negative on the above issues by adverting to certain statements of evidence of AW1 and referring to certain alleged discrepancies in the FIR without appreciating entire evidence of AW1 and AW2 on record properly and also not assigned valid reasons in not accepting their testimony.
The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.
The registration of FIR and filing of the chargesheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
Perhaps the non-pecuniary damages can be figured out by looking into the facts of each case by taking into account the nature of injuries and the aftermath.
It is required to be reminded to oneself that compensation in a case arising out of injury can never be granted on mathematical precision and invariably a good amount of guesswork is involved while determining the compensation in such cases.
Perhaps unlike in a fatal case, in a case involving bodily injury the victim is left to suffer throughout his life; and hence it becomes the bounden duty of the tribunal to award compensation to a victim of permanent disability so as to bring in sustainability and also to ensure that victim is not pushed to poverty.
19. In order to demonstrate the pecuniary loss suffered by him due to the injuries, the petitioner has led oral and documentary evidence.
It is very important to note that in his report the PW.3 has specifically mentioned that the petitioner is suffering with moderate severe disability and unable to attend his own bodily needs without assistant and unable to walk unassisted.
It is very important that the evidence of PW.3 is subjected to cross-examination by the learned counsel for the respondent.
The petitioner sustained with head injury which resulted in traumatic brain injury.
After the accident when the petitioner shifted to hospital he was unconscious.
When the person is unable to attend his own bodily needs we cannot expect that he is going to be a earning member in his family.
But it is very important to note that the person should not be left unattended or as a burden by the family.
A perusal of the injuries sustained, treatment taken and in view of the citation referred above, it is considered that though the petitioner is having 74% permanent physical disability ,his avocational disability is 100% because the evidence of Pw.3 is clear that the petitioner is unable to attend his own bodily needs without assistance and unable to walk unassisted.
This situation is nothing but making this tribunal to hold that the petitioner is unable to earn or to live independently hence, this disability is considered at 100%.
